periods.office: Minister of Housing and Local Government

metrics.justification: No personal corruption charge or conviction of record. The RM150m MyKiosk programme probe his ministry itself invited was reported by the anti-corruption commission (3 Jul 2025) to have found no criminal elements, abuse of power, or corruption; a separate alleged vote-buying matter was confirmed not under investigation (May 2024). No personal charge resulted.

citation.title: MACC probe found no criminal elements or abuse of power in MyKiosk project, ministry says

metrics.justification: Led the federal rehousing response to the 1 Apr 2025 Putra Heights gas-pipeline fire (~150 injured, dozens of homes destroyed): an RM46m federal-state recovery plan plus extra infrastructure funds, culminating in 18 families receiving keys to rebuilt homes on 4 Dec 2025, within about six months of works starting. Measurable, time-bound delivery (anchor 3).

citation.title: Govt allocates extra RM6mil for public infrastructure repairs in Putra Heights — Nga Kor Ming

metrics.justification: A mixed reform record: the Urban Renewal Bill reached first reading (21 Aug 2025) but was withdrawn (Jan 2026) before passage; the Residential Tenancy Act stayed in drafting; and reviving local-council elections, a longstanding cause, was indefinitely deprioritised. Reforms in progress with one signature item shelved (anchor 2).

citation.title: Govt withdraws Urban Renewal Bill to make further refinements

metrics.justification: The Urban Renewal Bill ran through a documented cross-bench process: 122 engagement sessions, three presentations to the Dewan Rakyat Special Select Committee, and approval by the National Council for Local Government, with on-record clause amendments responding to the committee. Engaged a cross-bench instrument, though the bill was later withdrawn (anchor 3).

citation.title: Ministry To Amend Urban Renewal Bill After Views Shared By Select Committee

metrics.justification: When the Urban Renewal Bill was withdrawn (Jan 2026), he explained on the record that the ministry would continue engagement and incorporate proposals before re-tabling, rather than concealing the climb-down. Reversal of a flagship bill explained openly, the Cabinet decision partly announced by another minister (anchor 3).

citation.title: Housing Ministry will continue to enhance URA before re-tabling, says Nga
